states.name: Chandigarh
states.blurb: Chandigarh eats Punjabi: hearty dhaba food, kulchas and lassi.
states.intro: Chandigarh eats Punjabi: hearty dhaba food, kulchas and lassi.

states.name: Delhi
states.blurb: Delhi is a food capital: Mughlai kebabs in Old Delhi, chaat everywhere and the Punjabi dishes made famous here.
states.intro: Delhi is a food capital: Mughlai kebabs in Old Delhi, chaat everywhere and the Punjabi dishes made famous here.

cities.name: Old Delhi
cities.blurb: Chandni Chowk: parathas, jalebis and kebabs.

states.name: Haryana
states.blurb: Earthy millets, buttermilk and home-style kadhi.
states.intro: Haryana's farm kitchens run on millets, greens, buttermilk and ghee. Simple, earthy food that is hard to find in restaurants elsewhere.

states.name: Himachal Pradesh
states.blurb: Mountain comfort: steamed siddu and the festive dham.
states.intro: Himachali food is mountain comfort: steamed breads, yoghurt-based gravies and the festive dham served on leaf plates at weddings and festivals.

cities.name: Kullu
cities.blurb: Valley of apple orchards and trout.

states.name: Jammu & Kashmir
states.blurb: Saffron, walnuts and the slow feast of wazwan.
states.intro: Kashmiri cooking is built around slow-cooked meats, saffron, dried ginger and fennel, with the grand wazwan feast at its heart. In Jammu, the food is heartier and more Punjabi in spirit.

states.name: Ladakh
states.blurb: High-altitude Ladakhi food is warm and filling: noodle soups, butter tea and barley.
states.intro: High-altitude Ladakhi food is warm and filling: noodle soups, butter tea and barley.

states.name: Punjab
states.blurb: Butter, tandoor and big-hearted portions.
states.intro: Punjab is the home of the tandoor, generous butter and slow-cooked dals. Food here is big-hearted, rich and made to share.

cities.name: Amritsar
cities.blurb: City of the Golden Temple and kulchas.

states.name: Uttar Pradesh
states.blurb: From Lucknow's royal Awadhi kebabs to Varanasi's chaat and Agra's petha, UP has some of India's richest food cities.
states.intro: From Lucknow's royal Awadhi kebabs to Varanasi's chaat and Agra's petha, UP has some of India's richest food cities.

cities.name: Lucknow
cities.blurb: City of Awadhi kebabs and biryani.

cities.name: Varanasi
cities.blurb: Holy city of chaat, kachori and paan.

states.name: Uttarakhand
states.blurb: Garhwali and Kumaoni food is hearty hill cooking with millets, lentils and local greens.
states.intro: Garhwali and Kumaoni food is hearty hill cooking with millets, lentils and local greens.

cities.name: Almora
cities.blurb: Kumaon town known for bal mithai.

states.name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
states.blurb: Coastal Gujarati and Portuguese-influenced cooking, with plenty of seafood.
states.intro: Coastal Gujarati and Portuguese-influenced cooking, with plenty of seafood.

states.name: Goa
states.blurb: Goan food blends Konkani coastal cooking with Portuguese influence: coconut, kokum, vinegar and the day's fresh catch.
states.intro: Goan food blends Konkani coastal cooking with Portuguese influence: coconut, kokum, vinegar and the day's fresh catch.

cities.name: Panaji
cities.blurb: Goa's capital, with old Portuguese-style kitchens.

states.name: Gujarat
states.blurb: Gujarati food is mostly vegetarian, with a sweet-salty-spicy balance and famous farsan (snacks).
states.intro: Gujarati food is mostly vegetarian, with a sweet-salty-spicy balance and famous farsan (snacks).

cities.name: Ahmedabad
cities.blurb: Snack capital with night markets like Manek Chowk.

states.name: Maharashtra
states.blurb: Maharashtra ranges from Mumbai's street food to Kolhapur's fiery curries and the sweet-sour cooking of Pune.
states.intro: Maharashtra ranges from Mumbai's street food to Kolhapur's fiery curries and the sweet-sour cooking of Pune.

cities.name: Mumbai
cities.blurb: Street-food capital: vada pav and pav bhaji.

cities.name: Pune
cities.blurb: Home of misal and Puneri sweets.

states.name: Rajasthan
states.blurb: Desert cooking makes the most of lentils, gram flour, ghee and dried beans, with royal meat dishes from the old kingdoms.
states.intro: Desert cooking makes the most of lentils, gram flour, ghee and dried beans, with royal meat dishes from the old kingdoms.

cities.name: Jaipur
cities.blurb: The Pink City of ghewar and pyaaz kachori.

states.name: Chhattisgarh
states.blurb: Chhattisgarh, the 'rice bowl of India', cooks simple rice-based dishes and tribal specialities.
states.intro: Chhattisgarh, the 'rice bowl of India', cooks simple rice-based dishes and tribal specialities.

states.name: Madhya Pradesh
states.blurb: The heart of India: Indore's legendary street food, Bhopal's Mughlai kebabs and simple Malwa cooking.
states.intro: The heart of India: Indore's legendary street food, Bhopal's Mughlai kebabs and simple Malwa cooking.

cities.name: Indore
cities.blurb: Street-food city of poha and Sarafa night market.

cities.name: Bhopal
cities.blurb: City of lakes and Mughlai food.

states.name: Bihar
states.blurb: Bihari food is wholesome and earthy, built on sattu, wheat and mustard oil, with famous festival sweets.
states.intro: Bihari food is wholesome and earthy, built on sattu, wheat and mustard oil, with famous festival sweets.

cities.name: Patna
cities.blurb: The capital, with litti stalls on every corner.

states.name: Jharkhand
states.blurb: Jharkhand's tribal kitchens cook with rice, local greens, mushrooms and mustard oil.
states.intro: Jharkhand's tribal kitchens cook with rice, local greens, mushrooms and mustard oil. Simple, earthy and rarely found outside the state.

cities.name: Ranchi
cities.blurb: The capital, with street snacks and tribal food markets.

states.name: Odisha
states.blurb: Odia food is subtle and comforting, with mustard, panch phoron, rice and the temple cooking of Puri.
states.intro: Odia food is subtle and comforting, with mustard, panch phoron, rice and the temple cooking of Puri.

cities.name: Puri
cities.blurb: Temple town of Lord Jagannath and its mahaprasad.

states.name: West Bengal
states.blurb: Bengal loves fish, rice and sweets.
states.intro: Bengal loves fish, rice and sweets. Mustard, poppy seeds and panch phoron flavour its cooking, and Kolkata is a street-food capital.

cities.name: Kolkata
cities.blurb: City of sweets, rolls and fish curries.

cities.name: Darjeeling
cities.blurb: Hill town of tea and momos.

states.name: Arunachal Pradesh
states.blurb: Arunachal's tribes cook simply with rice, bamboo shoots, smoked meats and local greens.
states.intro: Arunachal's tribes cook simply with rice, bamboo shoots, smoked meats and local greens.

states.name: Assam
states.blurb: Assamese food is light and flavourful, with sour fruits, herbs, fish and rice, and it is the land of Assam tea.
states.intro: Assamese food is light and flavourful, with sour fruits, herbs, fish and rice, and it is the land of Assam tea.

states.name: Manipur
states.blurb: Manipuri food is simple and healthy, with rice, fermented fish, fresh herbs and very little oil.
states.intro: Manipuri food is simple and healthy, with rice, fermented fish, fresh herbs and very little oil.

cities.name: Imphal
cities.blurb: The capital and its women-run Ima Market.

states.name: Meghalaya
states.blurb: Khasi, Jaintia and Garo cooking uses pork, rice, black sesame and fermented flavours.
states.intro: Khasi, Jaintia and Garo cooking uses pork, rice, black sesame and fermented flavours.

cities.name: Shillong
cities.blurb: Hill capital with a lively street-food scene.

states.name: Mizoram
states.blurb: Mizo food is simple and mild: boiled vegetables, rice, bamboo shoots and smoked meat.
states.intro: Mizo food is simple and mild: boiled vegetables, rice, bamboo shoots and smoked meat.

states.name: Nagaland
states.blurb: Naga food is bold and smoky, with smoked pork, bamboo shoots and the fiery king chilli (raja mircha).
states.intro: Naga food is bold and smoky, with smoked pork, bamboo shoots and the fiery king chilli (raja mircha).

states.name: Sikkim
states.blurb: Sikkim's Himalayan food is warming, with momos, noodle soups and fermented greens.
states.intro: Sikkim's Himalayan food is warming, with momos, noodle soups and fermented greens.

cities.name: Gangtok
cities.blurb: The capital, with momo stalls on MG Marg.

states.name: Tripura
states.blurb: Tripura's food uses fermented fish (berma), bamboo shoots and little oil.
states.intro: Tripura's food uses fermented fish (berma), bamboo shoots and little oil.

states.name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
states.blurb: Island food is all about fresh seafood and coconut.
states.intro: Island food is all about fresh seafood and coconut.

states.name: Andhra Pradesh
states.blurb: Fiery, tangy and generous: pickles, pulihora and slow-cooked curries.
states.intro: Andhra food is famous for its heat: Guntur chillies, tangy gongura and fiery pickles. It is also a land of temple sweets and coastal specialities.

cities.name: Annavaram
cities.blurb: Temple town on the Ratnagiri hill.

cities.name: Tirupati
cities.blurb: Home of the Tirumala temple and its laddu.

states.name: Karnataka
states.blurb: Dosas, bisi bele bath and coastal Mangalorean curries.
states.intro: From Udupi's temple kitchens to Mangaluru's coastal curries and the jowar rotis of the north, Karnataka has some of India's most varied food.

cities.name: Udupi
cities.blurb: Temple town that gave India its cafés.

states.name: Kerala
states.blurb: Coconut, curry leaves and the sea: appam, stew and banana-leaf sadya.
states.intro: Kerala cooks with coconut, curry leaves and the catch of the day. Try the backwater fish, Malabar biryani and a banana-leaf sadya.

cities.name: Palakkad
cities.blurb: Gateway between Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

states.name: Lakshadweep
states.blurb: Lakshadweep cooks with tuna, coconut and Malabar-style spices.
states.intro: Lakshadweep cooks with tuna, coconut and Malabar-style spices.

states.name: Puducherry
states.blurb: Tamil flavours with a French accent.
states.intro: Puducherry mixes Tamil home cooking with a French-colonial accent, from fiery fish curries to bakery-style bread pudding.

states.name: Tamil Nadu
states.blurb: Idli, dosa, Chettinad spice and temple-town sweets.
states.intro: Tamil Nadu gives India its idlis and dosas, but go further: peppery Chettinad curries, Madurai's jigarthanda and temple-town sweets.

cities.name: Tiruppur
cities.blurb: Textile city with its own biryani.

states.name: Telangana
states.blurb: Telangana is the home of Hyderabadi biryani and Nizami cooking, but its villages cook rustic, fiery food with millets, tamarind and sesame.
states.intro: Telangana is the home of Hyderabadi biryani and Nizami cooking, but its villages cook rustic, fiery food with millets, tamarind and sesame.

cities.name: Hyderabad
cities.blurb: The Nizams' city: biryani, haleem and Irani cafés.

dishes.name: Grilled lobster
dishes.description: Fresh lobster grilled with spices.

dishes.name: Fish curry
dishes.description: Coconut-based fish curry.

dishes.name: Coconut prawn curry
dishes.description: Prawns in coconut milk.

dishes.name: Pulihora
dishes.description: Tangy tamarind rice tempered with peanuts and curry leaves.
dishes.story: Pulihora is tamarind rice tempered with mustard seeds, peanuts, chillies and curry leaves. It is made at festivals and offered in temples across Andhra, and it travels well, so families pack it for journeys.

dishes.name: Annavaram prasadam
dishes.description: Sacred wheat, ghee and jaggery offering from the Annavaram temple.
dishes.story: The prasadam of the Satyanarayana Swamy temple in Annavaram is made with wheat rava, ghee, jaggery and cardamom, and is traditionally packed in a leaf. Pilgrims see it as a must, and many carry it home for family.

dishes.name: Tirupati laddu
dishes.description: The famous temple laddu from Tirumala.
dishes.story: Made in the temple kitchens of Tirumala and given to devotees after darshan, the Tirupati laddu is rich with ghee, cashews, raisins and cardamom. It has a Geographical Indication (GI) tag.

dishes.name: Bongulo chicken
dishes.description: Chicken slow-cooked inside bamboo over fire in Araku Valley.
dishes.story: In the Araku Valley, tribal cooks stuff marinated chicken into fresh bamboo and roast it over an open fire. The bamboo seals in the juices and adds a gentle, smoky aroma.

dishes.name: Gongura pacchadi
dishes.description: Sour sorrel-leaf chutney, Andhra's signature.
dishes.story: Gongura (sorrel leaves) is so loved in Andhra it is called the state's own pickle. The sour leaves are roasted and ground with chillies into a sharp chutney eaten with hot rice and ghee.

dishes.name: Kakinada kaaja
dishes.description: Crisp layered sweet soaked in sugar syrup, from Kakinada.
dishes.story: A crisp, layered sweet that is fried and then soaked in sugar syrup, so it is juicy inside. Kakinada's kaaja is famous across Andhra and is a favourite gift to take home.

dishes.name: Pootharekulu
dishes.description: Paper-thin rice sheets layered with ghee, sugar and nuts.
dishes.story: Pootharekulu, meaning 'coated sheets', are made from rice starch so thin it is almost see-through, layered with ghee, sugar or jaggery and nuts. Atreyapuram is famous for them.

dishes.name: Pesarattu upma
dishes.description: Green gram dosa wrapped around upma.
dishes.story: Pesarattu is a dosa made from whole green moong dal. In Andhra it is often folded around a spoonful of upma and served with ginger chutney, a filling breakfast.

dishes.name: Gongura mutton
dishes.description: Mutton cooked with tangy sorrel (gongura) leaves.
dishes.story: Tangy gongura leaves cut through rich mutton in this classic Andhra curry. It is spicy, sour and best eaten with steamed rice.

dishes.name: Aavakayi
dishes.description: Fiery raw-mango pickle with mustard and red chilli.

dishes.name: Andhra bhojanaalu
dishes.description: A full vegetarian Andhra meal: rice, dal, curries, pickles and more.

dishes.name: Appadaalu
dishes.description: Crisp lentil papads served with meals.

dishes.name: Badam milk
dishes.description: Warm or chilled almond milk with saffron and cardamom.

dishes.name: Bandar laddu
dishes.description: Melt-in-the-mouth gram-flour laddu from Machilipatnam.

dishes.name: Bobbatlu
dishes.description: Flatbread stuffed with sweet chana dal and jaggery.

dishes.name: Bongulo biriyani
dishes.description: Biryani cooked inside bamboo, from the Araku hills.

dishes.name: Boorelu
dishes.description: Fried dumplings with a sweet lentil and jaggery filling.

dishes.name: Chandrakaanthalu
dishes.description: Moong dal and coconut sweet, shaped like the moon.

dishes.name: Chepala pulusu
dishes.description: Tangy tamarind fish curry, Andhra style.

dishes.name: Crispy bhendi
dishes.description: Crisp-fried okra tossed with spices.

dishes.name: Dibba rotti
dishes.description: Thick, soft urad dal and rice bread cooked in a pan.

dishes.name: Dosakaya pacchadi
dishes.description: Yellow cucumber chutney with mustard and chilli.

dishes.name: Egg bonda
dishes.description: Boiled eggs dipped in gram-flour batter and fried.

dishes.name: Egg maggi
dishes.description: Street-style instant noodles tossed with egg and spices.

dishes.name: Ghee idly
dishes.description: Soft idlis soaked in ghee with podi.

dishes.name: Guntur mirchi
dishes.description: Famously hot Guntur chillies, stuffed and fried.

dishes.name: Gutthi vankaya
dishes.description: Baby aubergines stuffed with a peanut and spice masala.

dishes.name: Kaaju
dishes.description: Cashew sweet.

dishes.name: Kaaram dosa
dishes.description: Dosa spread with a fiery red chilli paste.

dishes.name: Katte pongal
dishes.description: Rice and moong dal with pepper, cumin and ghee.

dishes.name: Kheema undalu
dishes.description: Spiced minced-meat balls.

dishes.name: Kobbari bondalu
dishes.description: Coconut and jaggery sweet.

dishes.name: Kodi vepudu
dishes.description: Spicy Andhra chicken fry.

dishes.name: Madugula halwa
dishes.description: Rich, dark halwa from Madugula made with wheat and ghee.

dishes.name: Masala vada
dishes.description: Crunchy chana dal fritters with onion and spices.

dishes.name: Mirchi bajji

dishes.name: Mutton paya

dishes.name: Punugulu

dishes.name: Ragi sangati with natukodi pulusu
dishes.description: Finger-millet balls with spicy country-chicken curry.

dishes.name: Rava dosa

dishes.name: Sakinalu

dishes.name: Sweet mango pickle
dishes.description: Mango pickle with jaggery, sweet and spicy.

dishes.name: Sweet paan

dishes.name: Ulavachaaru

dishes.name: Undraalu

dishes.name: Khar

dishes.name: Pitha
dishes.description: Rice cakes made for Bihu, sweet or savoury.

dishes.name: Duck with ash gourd
dishes.description: Duck curry cooked with ash gourd, a Bihu favourite.

dishes.name: Aloo pitika
dishes.description: Mashed potato with mustard oil, onion and green chilli.

dishes.name: Litti chokha
dishes.description: Bihar's signature dish: roasted wheat balls stuffed with spiced sattu, with smoky aubergine-potato mash.

dishes.name: Tilkut
dishes.description: A crunchy sweet of pounded sesame and jaggery, made in Gaya each winter.

dishes.name: Khaja
dishes.description: A flaky, layered sweet soaked in sugar syrup, a speciality of Silao.

dishes.name: Thekua

dishes.name: Champaran mutton
dishes.description: Mutton slow-cooked with whole garlic and mustard oil in a sealed clay pot (handi).

dishes.name: Sattu paratha
dishes.description: Flatbread stuffed with spiced roasted gram flour.

dishes.name: Malpua
dishes.description: Sweet fried pancakes soaked in syrup, made during Holi.

dishes.name: Dal pitha
dishes.description: Rice-flour dumplings stuffed with spiced lentils and steamed.

dishes.name: Chole kulche
dishes.description: Spicy chickpeas with soft kulcha bread.

dishes.name: Amritsari fish
dishes.description: Battered, spiced fried fish.

dishes.name: Chila
dishes.description: A rice-flour pancake with chutney.

dishes.name: Fara
dishes.description: Steamed rice-flour dumplings, tempered with spices.

dishes.name: Bafauri
dishes.description: Steamed chana dal dumplings, oil-free.

dishes.name: Aamat
dishes.description: A tangy mixed-vegetable curry from Bastar.

dishes.name: Fish curry

dishes.description: A coastal fish curry with coconut and kokum, cooked the Daman way.

dishes.name: Prawn curry
dishes.state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
dishes.description: Prawns in a spiced gravy.

dishes.name: Chole bhature
dishes.description: Spicy chickpeas with fried bread, a Delhi favourite.

dishes.name: Paranthe wali gali parathas
dishes.description: Deep-fried stuffed parathas from Chandni Chowk's famous lane.

dishes.name: Nihari
dishes.description: Slow-cooked beef or mutton stew, eaten for breakfast.

dishes.name: Daulat ki chaat
dishes.description: A cloud-like winter sweet of whipped milk foam.

dishes.name: Aloo tikki chaat
dishes.description: Crisp potato patties with chutneys and yoghurt.

dishes.name: Butter chicken
dishes.description: Made famous in Delhi by Punjabi restaurateurs.

dishes.name: Goan fish curry rice
dishes.description: Fish in a tangy coconut and kokum curry with rice: what Goans call 'xit kodi', their daily meal.

dishes.name: Bebinca
dishes.description: A layered Goan cake of coconut milk, eggs, sugar and ghee, baked one layer at a time.

dishes.name: Chicken xacuti
dishes.description: Chicken in a complex gravy of roasted coconut, poppy seeds and spices.

dishes.name: Pork vindaloo
dishes.description: Pork in a hot, tangy sauce of vinegar, garlic and chillies, with Portuguese roots.

dishes.name: Prawn balchão
dishes.description: Prawns in a fiery, pickle-like sauce of chillies and vinegar.

dishes.name: Ros omelette
dishes.description: An omelette drowned in spicy chicken curry ('ros'), a Panaji street favourite.

dishes.name: Poi
dishes.description: Goa's soft wheat-bran bread, baked by local poders (bakers).

dishes.name: Sorpotel
dishes.description: A rich, spicy pork dish cooked with vinegar, made for feasts.

dishes.name: Dhokla
dishes.description: A soft, steamed savoury cake of fermented gram flour.

dishes.name: Gujarati thali
dishes.description: A full meal of dal, kadhi, vegetables, rotis, rice and sweets.

dishes.name: Undhiyu
dishes.description: A winter mixed-vegetable dish slow-cooked with fenugreek dumplings.

dishes.name: Fafda jalebi
dishes.description: Crisp gram-flour strips with sweet jalebis, a Sunday breakfast.

dishes.name: Khandvi
dishes.description: Thin rolls of gram flour and yoghurt with a mustard-seed tempering.

dishes.name: Locho
dishes.description: A soft, steamed gram-flour snack from Surat.

dishes.name: Thepla
dishes.description: Spiced fenugreek flatbread, the go-to travel food.

dishes.name: Siddu
dishes.description: Steamed wheat bun stuffed with walnuts or poppy seeds, served with ghee.
dishes.story: A steamed bread made with yeast and stuffed with walnuts, poppy seeds or lentils. Served hot with ghee, it is the comfort food of Kullu and Shimla.

dishes.name: Himachal dham
dishes.description: Festive feast served on leaf plates: madra, rajma, rice and sweet rice.
dishes.story: The dham is a festive meal cooked by traditional chefs called botis and served on leaf plates. It includes rice, madra, rajma and sweet rice.

dishes.name: Chana madra
dishes.description: Chickpeas slow-cooked in spiced yoghurt, a dham favourite.
dishes.story: Chickpeas cooked in a thick yoghurt gravy with ghee and whole spices. One of the stars of the dham.

dishes.name: Gucchi pulao
dishes.description: Fragrant rice cooked with rare wild morel mushrooms.
dishes.story: Rice cooked with gucchi, rare wild morel mushrooms foraged in the Himalayas. One of the most prized dishes of the hills.

dishes.name: Babru
dishes.description: Deep-fried flatbread stuffed with black gram paste.
dishes.story: A Himachali deep-fried bread stuffed with a paste of black gram. Crisp outside and soft inside, often eaten with tamarind chutney.

dishes.name: Mittha
dishes.description: Sweet saffron rice with dry fruits, the dham's dessert.
dishes.story: Sweet rice with saffron, raisins and dry fruits that ends the dham.

dishes.name: Aktori
dishes.description: Buckwheat pancake-style cake made in the hills for festivals.

dishes.name: Auraiya kaddu
dishes.description: Spiced pumpkin cooked in the Himachali home style.

dishes.name: Bhaturu
dishes.description: Fermented, fluffy Himachali bread, often eaten with madra.

dishes.name: Bhey
dishes.description: Lotus stem cooked with gram flour, onion and spices.

dishes.name: Charolia
dishes.description: A traditional Himachali festive preparation.

dishes.name: Chha gosht
dishes.description: Lamb cooked in a gram-flour and buttermilk gravy.

dishes.name: Kaddu ka khatta
dishes.description: Sweet-and-sour pumpkin with tamarind or dried mango.

dishes.name: Khatta
dishes.description: Tangy tamarind or chickpea gravy served as part of the dham.

dishes.name: Kodra roti
dishes.description: Finger-millet flatbread from the hills, eaten with ghee.

dishes.name: Kullu trout fish
dishes.description: Fresh river trout from Kullu, lightly spiced and pan-fried.

dishes.name: Luchis
dishes.description: Light, puffy deep-fried breads made with refined flour.

dishes.name: Patande
dishes.description: Thin Himachali pancakes, a Sirmaur favourite.

dishes.name: Sepu vadi
dishes.description: Lentil dumplings cooked in a spinach-based gravy.

dishes.name: Sidu
dishes.description: A variation of siddu, the stuffed steamed bread of the hills.

dishes.name: Thecha
dishes.description: Fiery coarse chutney of green chillies and garlic.

dishes.name: Tudkiya bhath
dishes.description: Spiced pulao from Chamba, cooked with lentils and potatoes.

dishes.name: Kadhi

dishes.story: Haryana's kadhi is a light, sour yoghurt and gram-flour curry, simmered slowly and eaten with rice or bajra roti.

dishes.name: Bajra khichdi

dishes.name: Dhuska

dishes.name: Litti chokha

dishes.name: Rogan josh

dishes.story: Tender lamb slow-cooked in a deep red gravy coloured by mild Kashmiri chillies and flavoured with fennel and dried ginger. A highlight of the wazwan.

dishes.name: Wazwan
dishes.description: The grand multi-course Kashmiri feast, cooked by master chefs.
dishes.story: Wazwan is Kashmir's grand feast of many courses, cooked by master chefs called wazas. It is served at weddings and shared from a large copper plate.

dishes.name: Gushtaba
dishes.description: Velvety mutton meatballs in a yoghurt gravy, the finale of wazwan.
dishes.story: Soft meatballs of finely pounded mutton cooked in a creamy yoghurt gravy. Gushtaba traditionally ends the wazwan.

dishes.name: Kahwa

dishes.story: Green tea brewed with saffron, cinnamon and cardamom, served with almonds. Kashmiris drink it through the day, especially in winter.

dishes.name: Dum aloo
dishes.description: Baby potatoes slow-cooked in a Kashmiri yoghurt and chilli gravy.
dishes.story: Small potatoes fried and slow-cooked in a yoghurt gravy with Kashmiri chillies and fennel. Rich, warming and vegetarian.

dishes.name: Modur pulav
dishes.description: Sweet saffron rice with ghee, dry fruits and cinnamon.
dishes.story: A sweet saffron rice cooked with ghee, sugar, dry fruits and cinnamon, made for celebrations.

dishes.name: Ambal
dishes.description: Sweet-and-sour pumpkin cooked with tamarind and jaggery.

dishes.name: Chilla

dishes.name: Kabargah

dishes.name: Kashmiri pulao

dishes.name: Khatte baingan

dishes.name: Seekh kebab
dishes.description: Spiced minced meat grilled on skewers.

dishes.name: Sheermal
dishes.description: Soft, slightly sweet saffron bread.

dishes.name: Tabak maaz
dishes.description: Lamb ribs braised in milk and spices, then fried crisp.

dishes.name: Tujji
dishes.description: Barbecued meat skewers, a Srinagar street favourite.

dishes.name: Masala dosa
dishes.description: Crisp dosa with a spiced potato filling.
dishes.story: A crisp golden dosa filled with spiced potato, served with coconut chutney and sambar. Bengaluru's old cafés made it famous.

dishes.name: Bisi bele bath
dishes.description: Hot rice, lentils and vegetables with a special spice powder.
dishes.story: Rice, lentils and vegetables cooked together with a special roasted spice powder and tamarind. The name means 'hot lentil rice'.

dishes.name: Mysore pak
dishes.description: Gram flour, ghee and sugar sweet from Mysore.
dishes.story: A rich sweet of gram flour, ghee and sugar, first made in the kitchens of Mysore Palace. It can be soft and fudgy or firm and porous.

dishes.name: Neer dosa
dishes.description: Delicate, lacy rice-batter crepes.
dishes.story: Neer means water: this delicate dosa is made from a thin rice batter, so it comes out soft and lacy. A coastal Karnataka favourite with chicken or fish curry.

dishes.name: Mangalorean fish curry
dishes.description: Fish in a red coconut and tamarind curry.
dishes.story: Fish simmered in a red curry of coconut, roasted chillies and tamarind. Mangaluru's coastal cooking at its best.

dishes.story: Rice tossed with lemon juice, turmeric, peanuts and curry leaves. Quick, tangy and made in every Karnataka home.

dishes.story: Appam is made from fermented rice batter swirled in a small pan, so the edges turn lacy and crisp while the centre stays soft. In Kerala it is eaten with vegetable or chicken stew.

dishes.name: Karimeen polichattu
dishes.description: Pearl-spot fish marinated and cooked in banana leaf.
dishes.story: Karimeen (pearl spot) is Kerala's state fish. It is coated in spicy masala, wrapped in banana leaf and pan-roasted, a speciality of the backwaters around Alappuzha and Kumarakom.

dishes.name: Puttu
dishes.description: Steamed cylinders of rice flour and coconut.
dishes.story: Puttu is rice flour and grated coconut steamed in layers inside a cylinder. It is a classic Kerala breakfast, often eaten with kadala (black chickpea) curry or banana.

dishes.name: Malabar biriyani
dishes.description: Fragrant short-grain biryani from Malabar.
dishes.story: Malabar biryani uses short-grain jeerakasala rice and is milder than other biryanis, fragrant with ghee, fried onions and whole spices. Kozhikode is its home.

dishes.name: Erissery
dishes.description: Pumpkin and lentils with roasted coconut.
dishes.story: Erissery is a comforting curry of pumpkin and lentils finished with coconut roasted until golden. It is a favourite part of the Onam sadya.

dishes.name: Achappam
dishes.description: Crisp, flower-shaped rose cookies.
dishes.story: Achappam, or rose cookies, are made by dipping a flower-shaped iron mould in rice batter and frying it. They are crisp, lightly sweet and made for Christmas and weddings.

dishes.story: A soft baked pudding of bread, milk and eggs, loved in Puducherry's bakeries since French times.

dishes.description: Basmati rice and marinated meat cooked together on dum (sealed slow cooking), fragrant with saffron and fried onions.

dishes.description: Wheat, lentils and meat slow-cooked into a rich, thick stew, famous in Hyderabad during Ramzan.

dishes.name: Irani chai with Osmania biscuit
dishes.description: Creamy, strong tea from Hyderabad's Irani cafés, dunked with buttery, slightly salty Osmania biscuits.

dishes.name: Qubani ka meetha
dishes.description: A Hyderabadi dessert of stewed dried apricots, often served with cream or ice cream.

dishes.name: Sarva pindi
dishes.description: A crisp, spicy rice-flour pancake with peanuts and chana dal, a Telangana tea-time snack.

dishes.description: Bread fried in ghee and soaked in saffron milk, a wedding favourite.

dishes.description: Green chillies in a tangy peanut, sesame and tamarind gravy, served with biryani.
